newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia police fire teargas at opposition protesters.
newsitem.headline: Zambia police fire teargas at opposition protesters.

text.p: Zambian police fired teargas cannisters into a multi-story building in the capital Lusaka on Wednesday to break up a demonstration by opposition leaders and supporters.
Witnesses said at least 20 people, including former president Kenneth Kaunda's aide Rabbison Chongo, were detained as people poured out of the smoke-filled building in an hour-long operation.
Chongo was detained last year by the government on suspicion of terrorism.
Business ground to a halt in the central city as apprehensive shop owners closed their premises and police sealed off roads leading to the inner city.
Earlier, hundreds of people scampered for safety when police fired teargas on the streets to break up the planned protest by an 11-party opposition coalition.
An opposition coalition led by former legal affairs minister Rodger Chongwe planned to demonstrate against the way in which general elections were held last year.
But protesters fled after police moved in, many seeking sanctuary in Freedom House, the building which houses Kaunda's United National Independence Party (UNIP).

Seven opposition parties boycotted last year's election, won by the Frederick Chiluba government which changed the constitution ahead of the poll, effectively banning some candidates from taking part.

Western donors cut aid to Zambia in protest against the move, but recently foreign funding has again started to flow back to the country after the government said it had made important economic reforms.
Donor-driven talks to get the opposition and government together for talks on political problems have however been unsuccessful.
The opposition coalition has in recent months resorted to a civil disobedience campaign to force the government to call for fresh elections using new electoral laws.
Protests appear to have gathered momentum after donors said they would lift the aid squeeze.
Opposition parties said foreign pressure would help force the government to address their concerns.
